motion_rule: the world flies at her: a pulley clothesline runs right to left all clip, she walks against it to stay in place; every action crosses the frame past the lens, never up or down; new shot size every beat, never wider than her head filling a third of frame, one action per beat
character: a slim grey turtle dove, pink breast, black neck ring, head stabbing the air
second_characters: A SWARM of crows crossing the lens; ONE sparrow, nothing on either
props: ONE red thread from her toe to a coin nest pegged on the moving line; ONE rolled banknote
prop_continuity: the thread runs taut; the sparrow takes the banknote at 1.65 and keeps it; coins only in the nest or crow claws
environment: sunlit yards packed with washing lines, wet sheets and pegged pillowcases sliding past the lens, a window hauling the line
light_events: blazing noon, wet sheets bouncing white light on her; at 7.25 the sun flares behind her

audio.language: Russian, lines verbatim; latin hints never spoken
audio.delivery: soft cooing female voice gone hard, preaching, biting each word, 4 syllables/sec
audio.pronunciation: ot-LO-zhish, CHOR-ny, pri-DYOT, CHOR-na-ya, DEN-gi, spa-SUT, TOL-ko, KRY-lya
audio.pacing: 0.95-2.70, 3.10-4.65 and 5.05-7.25 each one breath; after 7.25 not a word, sfx keep going
audio.lip_sync: her beak opens wide and shapes every syllable, throat swelling
audio.sfx: pulley squealing, sheets cracking, wingbeats, crow calls, coins ringing

timeline.a: she beats both wings full force and moves nowhere; a wet sheet rips off the lens
the thread drags her sideways along the wire; A SWARM tears past the lens
she runs against the moving line, ONE banknote in her beak; the sparrow darts past her, empty
she lunges neck out as the sparrow plucks the banknote from her beak and hauls it past the lens
the thread hauls her back and she lands splay-legged on the wire
A SWARM comes as a wall at the lens, shadows racing over the laundry, she ducks
she flails her wings at the crows and swings around her tied toe; the camera arcs around her
she hauls the nest down the line by the thread, the weight dragging her back
ONE crow knocks her wing at the lens and she reels sideways
she catches up on foot with the nest; the sparrow sails past the lens on a pillowcase
she hurls a handful of coins at the crows; the crows wheel onto the coins
she tears after the coins, the thread holds her; crows catch coins at the lens
she drags the emptying nest by the thread, hauled sideways past the lens
she throws her wings wide open, coins pouring from under them, she stays pinned
she dives at the camera and swings upside down on the thread filling the lens, wings hammering, beak snapping
she swings the empty nest down the line into the lens, nothing in it
she snaps her beak at the crows and misses; A SWARM hauls her coins across the lens
the line hauls her away backwards tied to the empty nest; the sparrow crosses the lens with her banknote

must_appear: the red thread runs from her toe to the nest; every word spoken, the last by 7.25; at 7.25 she hangs upside down filling the lens, wings hammering, alive and furious; the crows carry her coins off
